commits.message:
Align profile closing sentences for bilingual end-of-episode enforcement.

This adds deterministic final sentence instructions to Ship It and updates Arxiv/Ship It closing text so EN/FR adaptation and trim markers are consistent across both profile families.

Made-with: Cursor

Refresh arXiv profile in static to the structured YAML schema.

This aligns the live notebook profile source with the generator's current structured parser so adapter=arxiv sync and full EN/FR generation pipelines run successfully.

Made-with: Cursor

Migrate arXiv profile to structured schema with 3 segments.

Preserve the original arXiv guidance while adapting it to speaker_profiles/podcast_profile format and removing duplicated language/speaker-overlap instructions from briefing content.

Made-with: Cursor

Migrate Ship It profile to structured YAML format for generator sync.

Switch to split speaker_profiles/podcast_profile schema so profile sync is compatible with the new generator parser and Notebook API payload expectations.

Made-with: Cursor

Revert ShipIt profile to known-good prompt template.

Restore the previous text prompt format used by sync so speaker and episode profiles are created reliably.

Restore parser-compatible ShipIt profile format.

Revert ShipIt profile to the known-good prompt format so sync can recreate speaker and episode profiles without setup errors.

Fix ShipIt speaker profile mapping for sync.

Keep the internal speaker profile reference expected by the profile parser while preserving three segments to avoid speaker profile creation failures.

Tune ShipIt profile linkage and segment count.

Set ShipIt episode profile to three segments and point the speaker profile reference to tech_experts_en for consistent sync mapping.

Update ShipIt profile to structured 3-speaker format.

Switch the ShipIt prompt to explicit speaker and podcast profile blocks so generation uses the new host/practitioner/researcher setup with fixed five-segment flow.

Relax arxiv podcast counting procedure into policy guidance.

Replace rigid step-by-step instructions with rules that distinguish attempted generation from AWS-published uploads so agents can adapt queries while prioritizing publish evidence.

Made-with: Cursor

Fix podcast name extraction in arxiv ops skill.

Use selected-articles.selected_articles[].name as the source of truth and explicitly prevent reporting blog-podcast workflow IDs as user-facing names.

Made-with: Cursor

Fix arxiv-podcast-ops skill: filter by date, check article selection

The skill was counting ALL publish pods across all days instead of
filtering to the requested time period. Now uses date-filtered
workflow listing and also checks daily-arxiv-podcast status.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add arxiv-podcast-ops skill to ask/skills for K8s chat agent

Copy the podcast ops skill into the ask agent's skill directory so
the orchestrator-chat can load it when handling podcast-related
questions.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Restructure skill: podcast counting is the first section, not buried

Agent kept counting daily-arxiv-podcast pods as podcasts despite the
warning. Restructured so the counting recipe is the very first section
with CRITICAL warning about daily-arxiv-podcast. Renamed architecture
to clearly label the three pipeline stages and mark which ones produce
audio and which don't.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Clarify workflow naming to prevent miscounting podcasts

Agent confused daily-arxiv-podcast (article selector, zero audio)
with actual podcast generation (blog-podcast-* workflows). Added a
prominent IMPORTANT section explaining the distinction and updated
the "how many podcasts" recipe to explicitly filter on blog-podcast-*
workflows only.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add quick-answer recipes to arxiv-podcast-ops skill

The agent was unable to answer "how many podcasts today" because the
skill only documented architecture and debugging steps but not direct
answers to common operational questions. Add a Quick Answers section
at the top with copy-paste commands for counting episodes, checking
failures, listing candidates, RSS feed URLs, and active profile info.
Also broaden the description trigger terms.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Link podcast profiles to arxiv-podcast-ops skill

Add Podcast Profiles section to SKILL.md documenting the active
(shipit) and legacy (notebook) profiles with speakers, structure,
and closing scripts. Add detailed profile reference to reference.md
covering how profiles flow through sync-notebook into Open Notebook
and how to change the active profile.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add arxiv-podcast-ops Cursor skill for pipeline investigation

Skill provides the agent with architecture overview, debugging workflows,
known failure patterns, manual operation commands, and full reference for
the Arxiv podcast generation pipeline (Argo Workflows, Open Notebook,
Blog API, Zeus, S3/CloudFront).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Remove get_tracks/get_artists from allowed tools to prevent rate limiting
Update spotify skill: classify takes playlist data directly, no extra API calls

Add spotify skill for playlist management via MCP

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

delete skills: use delete_application tool with HIL confirmation

delete-app: rewritten to use the new delete_application tool which handles
K8s + NAS cleanup atomically with interrupt()-based user confirmation.
delete-database: updated to prefer delete_application, kept manual fallback
for standalone databases.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

build-application: update allowed-tools with utility tools, exclude edit_file

Space-delimited format per deepagents convention. Added read_file, ls,
grep, glob, write_file for diagnostics and fixes. edit_file intentionally
excluded — enforced at runtime by sandbox guard.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

build-application: document framework param and auto-test behavior

build_back and build_front now accept a framework parameter and
automatically run the generated test suite. Updated SKILL.md steps
3 and 3b to reflect the new API and instruct the agent to check
tests_passed output.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Update build-application skill: mandatory frontend asset verification in Step 7

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

skills: use build_back + build_front tools in build-application

Steps 3/3b now call build_back and build_front to scaffold FastAPI
backend and React frontend from entity definitions. Step 3c allows
write_file customizations. Added both tools to allowed-tools list.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

skills: add deploy_application tool refs, fix DB duplication guard

- build-application: Step 4 now checks for existing connection string
  before calling create_database. Step 6 uses deploy_application tool
  instead of manual kubectl manifests. Step 7 simplified since the tool
  runs verification internally.
- deploy-to-k8s: added deploy_application as preferred tool for standard
  deployments, manual kubectl for updates/debugging/custom operations.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

build-application skill: rewrite with software engineer mindset

Reframe the skill to set the LLM in a software engineer mindset that
inherently distinguishes building (developing code from scratch,
packaging into an artifact) from deploying (putting an artifact on
infrastructure). The previous version jumped into procedural steps
without establishing this mental model, causing the agent to confuse
"build" with "deploy" and fail on empty workspaces.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Strengthen verification: test all layers (DB, API, frontend) and require ingress testing

- build-application: Step 7 now explicitly requires testing DB, REST API,
  and frontend as separate layers, with frontend testing through the
  external ingress URL (not just localhost)
- verify-deployment: Frontend-via-ingress is now mandatory when an ingress
  exists, with troubleshooting guidance for common failures

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add report_facts instructions to build-application and access-database skills

Skills now instruct agents to call the report_facts tool after
provisioning databases or building images, ensuring structured facts
(credentials, URLs, ports) are persisted for downstream tasks.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Remove ask_human from delete-app and no-human-dependency skills

All user confirmation is now handled by submit_plan at orchestrator
level. ask_human is deprecated (auto-approves). Subagents proceed
directly after orchestrator obtains approval.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Update build-application skill for profile system

Remove ask_human requirement — plan approval now handled by orchestrator
via submit_plan. Subagents proceed directly with execution. Add explicit
tool usage rules (create_database, build_and_push).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add verify-deployment skill and mandate post-deploy testing

- New skill: verify-deployment — requires health, DB, API, frontend,
  and ingress checks after every deployment or fix
- Updated build-application: added Step 5 (mandatory verification)
- Updated deploy-to-k8s: added post-deploy verification section

Prevents declaring success without actually testing the app works.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add inspect-app skill: always check K8s AND NAS when inspecting apps

Ensures the agent checks both Kubernetes resources and NAS databases
when the user asks about an application's presence or status.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add build-application skill: mandatory planning before coding

Requires the orchestrator to present a detailed plan (modules, technologies,
architecture, deployment steps) via ask_human and get user confirmation
before writing any code.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Update delete-app skill to check both K8s and NAS databases

Unified deletion procedure: when deleting an app, always check and clean up
both Kubernetes resources AND any associated PostgreSQL database on the NAS.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Remove 5 tool-doc skills merged into LangChain tool docstrings

Merged content from infra-catalog, registry-lookup, database-provisioning,
build-image, and session-filesystem skills into their respective tool
docstrings in backend/main.py. Skills now only contain domain knowledge
and multi-step procedures.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add 9 new skills: split orchestrator prompt into skills

New skills extract domain knowledge from the monolithic system prompt:
- infra-catalog, registry-lookup, database-provisioning
- sandbox-runtime, session-filesystem, kubernetes-ops
- github-ops, app-conventions, no-human-dependency

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add delete-app and delete-database skills

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Update build-image skill to use build_and_push MCP tool

The new build_and_push tool atomically handles Docker daemon startup,
image build, local smoke test, and registry push. If the smoke test
fails, the push is blocked — agents cannot skip it.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add local smoke test and early crash detection to agent skills

- build-image: mandatory docker run smoke test before pushing to registry
- deploy-to-k8s: check pod state after 15s instead of blind rollout wait

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Strengthen TLS/HTTPS requirement in deploy-to-k8s skill

Make cert-manager + Let's Encrypt mandatory in ALWAYS section and
add explicit NEVER rule against non-TLS ingresses.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Add agent skills for ask platform

Four SKILL.md playbooks: build-image (Docker), deploy-to-k8s,
manage-nas (Synology SSH), access-database (PostgreSQL).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Create podcast profile for 'Ship it with AI'

Add a generic podcast profile for 'Ship it with AI' featuring roles for Jamie and Marc, along with detailed conversation rules and episode structure.

Add podcast profile for podcast-generator pipeline

Shared English base profile used by both arxiv and mattermost pipelines.
The generator derives per-language variants at runtime.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Merge branch 'main' of github.com:nblotti/Pheidippides into main
